short_summary: Bandung is a highland city in West Java known for Sundanese cuisine, Art Deco architecture, volcanic landscapes, and factory outlet shopping.
method_note: Agent reported WebFetch unavailable · evidence from WebSearch result snippets citing Wikipedia + indonesia.travel + travel guides. One stale-prone claim about Husein Sastranegara flagged for lower confidence.

food.claim: Batagor and siomay, savory fried fish cakes served with spicy peanut sauce, are signature street foods.
Sundanese cuisine emphasizes fresh raw vegetables in dishes like lalab and karedok with sambal.
Punclut district food stalls serve traditional Sundanese dishes including nasi timbel and ketan bakar.

shopping.claim: Pasar Baru Trade Center, founded 1884, offers textiles, batik, fashion, and Muslim clothing with haggling culture.
Rumah Mode Factory Outlet sells original discounted items with Balinese architectural design.
Bandung's textile factories on outskirts sell sisa export items at factory outlets with local designer linkages.

attractions.claim: Braga Street features well-preserved colonial Art Deco architecture earning Bandung the nickname 'Paris of Java.'
Bandung contains one of the world's largest collections of Art Deco-Nieuwe Bouwen tropical colonial buildings.
Tangkuban Perahu volcano crater north of city offers hiking and hot springs tourist experiences.
Bandung Institute of Technology, designed 1918 by Henri Maclaine Pont, blends Indonesian vernacular with modern architecture.

transport.claim: Argo Parahyangan train connects Bandung Station to Jakarta Gambir in approximately 3.5 hours.
Whoosh high-speed rail connects Padalarang/Tegalluar stations to Jakarta Halim in about 35 minutes.

excluded_claims.claim: Husein Sastranegara International Airport reactivated June 2026 serves domestic and international flights.
